{{short description|American mathematician}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=July 2025}}
'''David P. Sumner''' is an American mathematician known for his research in [[graph theory]]. He formulated [[Sumner's conjecture]] that [[tournament (graph theory)|tournaments]] are [[universal graph]]s for [[polytree]]s in 1971,<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Kühn | first1 = Daniela | author1-link = Daniela Kühn
 | last2 = Mycroft | first2 = Richard
 | last3 = Osthus | first3 = Deryk
 | arxiv = 1010.4430
 | doi = 10.1112/plms/pdq035
 | issue = 4
 | journal = [[Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society]] | series = Third Series
 | mr = 2793448 | zbl=1218.05034 
 | pages = 731–766
 | title = A proof of Sumner's universal tournament conjecture for large tournaments
 | volume = 102
 | year = 2011| s2cid = 119169562 }}.</ref> and showed in 1974 that all [[claw-free graph]]s with an even number of vertices have [[perfect matching]]s.<ref>{{Citation
 | last1 = Faudree | first1 = Ralph | author1-link = Ralph Faudree
 | last2 = Flandrin | first2 = Evelyne
 | last3 = Ryjáček | first3 = Zdeněk
 | doi = 10.1016/S0012-365X(96)00045-3
 | mr = 1432221
 | issue = 1–3
 | journal = [[Discrete Mathematics (journal)|Discrete Mathematics]]
 | pages = 87–147
 | title = Claw-free graphs — A survey
 | volume = 164
 | year = 1997| doi-access = free
 }}.</ref> He and [[András Gyárfás]] independently formulated the [[Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture]] according to which, for every [[Tree (graph theory)|tree]] ''T'', the ''T''-free graphs are [[χ-bounded]].

Sumner earned his doctorate from the [[University of Massachusetts Amherst]] in 1970, under the supervision of [[David J. Foulis]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=7998}}</ref> He is a distinguished professor emeritus at the [[University of South Carolina]].<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.math.sc.edu/david-sumner|title=Faculty & Staff Directory: David Sumner|publisher=University of South Carolina Department of Mathematics|accessdate=2015-08-30}}.</ref>
